name: opencode-unofficial
description: Chat with OpenCode in the VS Code sidebar. Sessions live on your OpenCode server and keep running when you close the editor. Native diffs, terminal, voice input. Unofficial — not affiliated with the OpenCode team.

opencode.serverUrl.markdownDescription:
Address of an OpenCode server to connect to, for example one running on another computer. **Leave empty** to use OpenCode on this computer (the extension starts its shared service if needed; no password required).

Examples:
- `http://192.168.1.10:4096`: a computer on your network (`4096` is OpenCode's default port)
- `http://my-server.tail1234.ts.net:4096`: over Tailscale
- `https://opencode.example.com`: behind a domain with HTTPS (no port needed)

`http://` is added when you leave it out. Without a port, `http` uses 80 and `https` uses 443. If the server has a password (`OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`), run **OpenCode: Set Server Password**.

opencode.cliPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `opencode` executable. Leave empty to look it up on `PATH`, then in `~/.opencode/bin`.

opencode.transcript.collapseCompletedSte.markdownDescription: When a turn finishes, fold its steps under one `N steps completed` line above the final answer.

opencode.transcript.expandToolDetails.markdownDescription: Show tool details (input, output, errors) expanded by default.

opencode.transcript.showReasoning.markdownDescription: How the model's reasoning is shown in the transcript.

opencode.transcript.fontSize.markdownDescription: Transcript font size in px. `0` uses the larger of `#chat.editor.fontSize#` and 14.

opencode.todo.defaultExpanded.markdownDescription: Show the task list panel expanded by default. It only appears when the agent uses the `todowrite` tool (OpenCode setting `experimental.todo`, which this extension never changes).

opencode.notifications.enabled.markdownDescription: Show VS Code notifications when OpenCode needs your attention or finishes work. Master switch for the settings below.

opencode.notifications.attention.markdownDescription: Notify when a session asks for a permission or a question (`permission.asked`, `form.created`).

opencode.notifications.completed.markdownDescription: Notify when a turn finishes in a root session.

opencode.notifications.failed.markdownDescription: Notify when a turn fails in a root session.

opencode.notifications.workers.markdownDescription: Also notify when a worker (child session) finishes or fails.

opencode.notifications.shells.markdownDescription: Also notify when a background shell of this project exits.

enumDescriptions: Stay quiet while this window is focused and the session is visible in the panel.
Notify even when the session is on screen.
opencode.notifications.whenFocused.markdownDescription: Whether to notify while the VS Code window is focused and the session is visible in the OpenCode panel.

enumDescriptions: Also ask the OS for attention through the OpenCode Voice companion when this window is not focused: the taskbar button flashes (Windows), the window is marked as needing attention (Linux X11), or an OS notification appears (macOS).
VS Code notifications only.
opencode.notifications.os.markdownDescription: Delivery channel. A VS Code notification is always shown. `auto` also asks the operating system for attention through the OpenCode Voice companion when this window is not focused: the taskbar button flashes (Windows), the window is marked as needing attention (Linux X11) or an OS notification appears (macOS). `off` shows VS Code notifications only.

enumDescriptions: Open a terminal for each shell command when it starts, without taking keyboard focus.
Create the terminal but do not reveal it. Use Show terminal on the tool line.
Do not mirror shell commands into terminals.
opencode.terminal.reveal.markdownDescription: Mirror OpenCode shell commands into read-only VS Code terminals. The command itself runs on the OpenCode server.

enumDescriptions: One terminal per session, named `OpenCode: <session title>`. Every command is appended as its own block. A command that starts while another one of the session is still running gets an extra terminal (`#2`), which later commands reuse.
A new terminal for every command, named `OpenCode: <command>`.
opencode.terminal.mode.markdownDescription: How shell commands are shown in terminals. Ctrl+C in a terminal stops only the command that is running, after asking. Closing a terminal never stops the command: it keeps running on the server.

opencode.terminal.maxOpen.markdownDescription: Most OpenCode terminals kept open. When there are more, the least recently used idle one is closed. A terminal with a running command is never closed.

opencode.view.minWidth.markdownDescription: Minimum width in px the OpenCode view tries to open with. Best effort: VS Code has no API for the side bar width. `0` turns this off.

One multilingual model (NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5, about 693 MB with the speech engine) covers English and about 28 other languages; Bangla is an optional extra pack. Downloaded once, the first time you use it. Choose languages with OpenCode: Choose Voice Language.
Cloud, with your own paid Soniox key: better accuracy, mixed languages, many languages.
opencode.voice.engine.markdownDescription:
Which speech engine voice input uses.

- `local`: free, offline, runs on this computer. Speaks the current language of `opencode.voice.localLanguages` (English by default). Downloads once, the first time you use it: the multilingual model (about 693 MB with the speech engine; one model for English and about 28 other languages) or, for Bangla, a separate pack (about 179 MB).
- `soniox`: cloud, with your own paid key (**OpenCode: Set Voice API Key (Soniox)**). Better accuracy, mixed languages, many languages (`opencode.voice.languages`).

opencode.voice.localLanguages.markdownDescription:
The languages you speak with the on-device engine (`opencode.voice.engine`: `local`), at most `opencode.voice.maxLanguages`. **The first one is the current language and the only one that records**; one model runs at a time. Switch with **OpenCode: Switch Voice Language** or by clicking the language label next to the mic in the prompt box. Easier than editing: run **OpenCode: Choose Voice Language**, which groups languages by download and marks what is already on this computer.

When this setting is not set, the old single setting `opencode.voice.localLanguage` is used as the list. Choosing or switching languages writes this setting.

opencode.voice.maxLanguages.markdownDescription:
How many languages can be active at once in `opencode.voice.localLanguages` (default 2). What it costs:

- Languages that share the multilingual model (every language except Bangla) cost nothing extra: one download (about 682 MB), one model.
- Each extra separate pack costs its download on disk: Bangla is about 168 MB.
- Only one model is loaded while you record, so RAM and CPU do not grow with this number (the multilingual model needs about 1 GB of RAM while you record).
- Switching to a language from another pack reloads the model: about 2 seconds (measured 1.6 to 1.7 s to load the multilingual model; the Bangla models are smaller). Switching between languages of the same pack needs no reload of the files, only a new recording.

Packs you no longer use are never deleted by themselves: **OpenCode Voice: Remove Downloaded Languages** deletes them.

enumDescriptions: English (multilingual model).
Bangla (separate pack).
opencode.voice.localLanguage.deprecationMessage: Use opencode.voice.localLanguages (a list; the first entry is the current language). This single value is still read while localLanguages is not set.
opencode.voice.localLanguage.markdownDescription: **Deprecated**: use `opencode.voice.localLanguages`. The single on-device language of test builds before 0.3.7 (`en` or `bn`). It is still honoured while `opencode.voice.localLanguages` is not set, and then becomes the first entry of the list. Choosing or switching a language writes `localLanguages` and this value is no longer used.

opencode.voice.localThreads.markdownDescription: CPU threads the on-device model uses. The default (2) is the fastest we measured with the multilingual model (real-time factor about 0.32; 1 thread about 0.45; 4 threads about 0.8, slower, because the threads fight over memory). Change it only when you measured a gain on your computer.

opencode.voice.languages.markdownDescription: Languages you speak, as ISO codes (for example `bn`, `en`, `hi`). Soniox uses them as hints; it still hears other languages. Only for the `soniox` engine: the on-device engine uses `opencode.voice.localLanguages`.

opencode.voice.model.markdownDescription: Soniox real-time model for voice input (engine `soniox` only).

scripts.build: bun run build:ext && bun run build:webview
scripts.watch: bun run watch:ext & bun run watch:webview & wait
scripts.watch:webview: vite build --watch & vite build --config vite.settings.config.ts --watch & wait
scripts.typecheck: tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && svelte-check --tsconfig tsconfig.webview.json && svelte-check --tsconfig tsconfig.settings.json
